Beyond the Basics: Mastering Microsoft Teams

Microsoft Teams serves as a central hub for over 320 million monthly active users, yet many rely solely on basic messaging and video calling. To improve efficiency in remote and hybrid environments, several underutilized features are available to help manage time, reduce distractions, and organize workflows.

1. Managing Meeting Duration with Countdown Timers

Meetings often run over their allotted time, which can disrupt a productive workday. Introduced in mid-2025, the countdown timer feature allows organizers to set a visible clock in the top-left corner of a meeting. The timer can be set for up to 100 minutes and provides visual cues—turning red and eventually flashing—as the time concludes. Note that this feature is currently limited to scheduled meetings and does not apply to live events or spontaneous calls.

2. Eliminating Distractions with Voice Isolation

To assist users in noisy environments, Teams offers a voice isolation feature powered by AI. By recording a brief voice profile through the 'Recognition' settings, the app can differentiate your voice from background noise. During a call, this can be toggled on via the microphone dropdown menu, ensuring that only your speech is transmitted clearly.

3. Reviewing Conversations with Live Transcription

Since 2021, Microsoft Teams has included live transcription, which captures spoken dialogue in near real-time. This allows participants to review what was said both during and after a meeting. The system can differentiate between speakers, and Microsoft states that this data is not used to train its AI models. Users can turn off speaker attribution via their accessibility settings if they prefer to remain anonymous.

4. Tracking Unfinished Thoughts with Message Drafts

Starting in March 2026, Teams introduced a specific area to manage unsent drafts. Users can find a list of partially written messages in the left-hand panel of the chat interface. This allows you to quickly locate and resume interrupted messages without hunting through multiple conversation threads, reducing the risk of losing important information.

*Verify these features by checking your specific Teams version or consulting with your IT administrator, as organizational policies may restrict access to certain tools.*
